Spec review companion · #151 · snapshot e284a60 · 2026-10-27

Fix release run step 4 of v1.0.23

Read the open sections in about ten minutes. Everything closed is a look-up. A file:line chip jumps to the source line at the bottom, for when a claim needs checking.

Bug #151

The change

A Copilot task whose prompt held a double quote failed before Copilot started. The plugin names the session after the start of the prompt, and Copilot CLI refuses a name with a ". assessment:40

The fix puts a space in place of each " and ASCII control character in the name; the prompt is unchanged. fix:10

1code file fix:18
4tests added fix:36
6checks run, all as expected test:18
1deviation fix:68

Root cause

The name kept every character of the prompt but white space; Codex's app server takes any name, Copilot CLI does not. assessment:64

Remediation

One filter in buildTaskThreadName, before the 56-character cut. assessment:71

How it works

What Copilot CLI refuses
  • A double quote. assessment:30
  • An ASCII control character, also a tab. assessment:31
  • More than 100 UTF-16 units; the plugin's name is at most 80. assessment:32
  • An empty name; the plugin falls back to the bare prefix. assessment:33

Examples

Before, real CLI

Say "ok" as a read-only task: exit 1, "Session name must not contain double quotes." test:18

After, real CLI

The same task: exit 0, answer ok. test:19

The fake CLI

Now refuses the same names as Copilot CLI 1.0.95, so every task test checks the name. fix:19

The prompt

Copilot still gets the quotes; only the name loses them. fix:36

What breaks for someone else

WhoWhat changesWhere listed
A user with a quoted task promptThe task runs; its session name has spaces for the quotesfix:10
Existing session namesNothing; only new tasks changeassessment:132
UpstreamNothing; Codex takes any nameassessment:133
Delivery
  1. Patch release 1.0.24, whose entry also brings the unpublished 1.0.23 change. fix:23

What to check before approving

  1. A one-string prompt still loses its quotes. That is #111, main's behaviour; the read-only test passes --fresh to stay off that path. fix:68
  2. The probe ran on Windows only. CI checks the rules through the fake CLI. assessment:128
  3. A later Copilot CLI may refuse more. The release run would show it. assessment:130

Look-ups

Glossary
  • Session name: the --name Copilot shows for a session, so you can find it.
  • Control character: U+0000 to U+001F and U+007F, such as a tab.

# Bug Assessment: a task whose prompt holds a double quote fails before Copilot starts - **Slug**: 151-safe-session-name- **Created**: 2026-10-27- **Source**: pasted text (issue #151, with a probe of Copilot CLI 1.0.95 made on 2026-10-27)- **Verdict**: valid- **Severity**: high ## Report (verbatim or summarized) Issue #151, "Fix release run step 4 of v1.0.23". Release run step 4 of v1.0.23 started a background`task --write` with the prompt `Add the comment line "// Checked by the release run." at the top ofmath.js. Change no other file.` It failed at once, before Copilot ran: ```textCopilot stopped before it sent a result (exit 1).Session name must not contain double quotes.``` `buildTaskThreadName` (`plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/copilot.mjs:89`) makes the session name from thefirst 56 characters of the prompt, and `copilot.mjs:212` passes it as `--name=<name>`. Copilot CLI1.0.95 refuses a name with a `"`. The same task without the quotes completed. The defect is olderthan v1.0.23, which changed only the modes of the state folders and job files (#126). The probe ran the real Copilot CLI 1.0.95 on Windows with `--model=no-such-model-xyz`, so a namethat passes fails at the model check and no model call runs. `--name` refuses: | Name holds | Copilot CLI says || --- | --- || `"` | Session name must not contain double quotes. || tab, U+0001, U+007F | Session name must not contain control characters. || more than 100 UTF-16 units (60 emoji) | Session name must be 100 characters or less. || nothing | Session name cannot be empty. | It accepts `'`, a backtick, `\`, `$ % < > | & ; : / #`, non-ASCII letters, emoji, U+2028, the C1controls U+0085 and U+009F, a lone surrogate, a leading `-`, and exactly 100 characters. ## Symptom A `/copilot:rescue` or `task` whose prompt holds a double quote, or an ASCII control character thatis not white space, in its first 56 characters fails before Copilot starts, in the foreground andthe background. Expected: the task runs whatever its prompt holds, and the session name still startswith the start of the prompt. ## Reproduction 1. In a git repo, run `node plugins/copilot/scripts/copilot-companion.mjs task 'Say "hi".'` with the   real Copilot CLI 1.0.95.2. The task fails with "Session name must not contain double quotes." and no Copilot turn runs.3. The same with `Say hi.` completes. ## Suspected Code Paths - `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/copilot.mjs:89` `buildTaskThreadName`: puts `shorten(prompt, 56)`  after the prefix `Copilot Companion Task: ` with no filter.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/copilot.mjs:78` `shorten`: folds white space runs into one space and  cuts to 56, so a tab or newline never reaches the name, but `"` and the other ASCII controls do.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/copilot.mjs:212`: passes the name as `--name=<name>`.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/copilot-companion.mjs:599`: the only caller, through  `buildPersistentTaskThreadName`; a resume passes no name. ## Root Cause Hypothesis The name comes from the prompt with only white space folded. Codex's app server takes any threadname, so upstream never filtered it; Copilot CLI checks `--name` and refuses `"` and ASCII controlcharacters. The other two rules hold already: the name is at most 24 + 56 = 80 UTF-16 units, and itfalls back to the bare prefix, so it is never empty. Confidence: high (the probe shows each rule). ## Proposed Remediation **Preferred**: in `buildTaskThreadName`, replace each `"` and each ASCII control character(U+0000 to U+001F and U+007F) in the prompt with a space before `shorten`, so `shorten` folds thespaces and the 56-character cut and the empty fallback stay as they are. The prompt that Copilotreceives does not change; only the session name does. One line, in the one place where the name isbuilt. **Alternatives**: - Remove the characters instead of replacing them: `"word"` stays readable either way, but  `a\u0001b` would join two words. A space is closer to what `shorten` already does with white space.- Drop `--name` for tasks: no failure, but the user can no longer find the task's session in Copilot  by its name, which the issue asks to keep. **Files likely to change**: - `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/copilot.mjs` (the filter, and the header comment)- `tests/fake-copilot-fixture.mjs` (the fake CLI refuses a name as the real one does)- `tests/runtime-task.test.mjs` (task runs with such prompts)- `README.md` (a "Differences from the Codex plugin" bullet)- `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md`, and the version files through `npm run bump-version -- 1.0.24` **Tests to add or update**: - The fake CLI (a template string in `tests/fake-copilot-fixture.mjs`, so each `\` in its regular  expressions is doubled) checks `--name` like Copilot CLI 1.0.95: a `"` or an ASCII control  character, more than 100 UTF-16 units, or an empty value fails with exit 1 and the real message  on stderr, before any event. The check runs after the run record is written, so a test sees the  refused name in `runs()`. Every run through the fake CLI that passes `--name` is then checked: in  `tests/runtime-task.test.mjs` the task tests (for example the ones at lines 95, 117 and 195).  `tests/copilot.test.mjs:97` builds the arguments without the fake CLI and is not covered by it.- Direct runs of the fake CLI with each refused name (`a"b`, a tab, U+0001, U+007F, 101 characters,  60 emoji, empty) give exit 1, the matching message and no event; `'`, non-ASCII and exactly 100  characters pass. These check the fake CLI's rules themselves.- A foreground `task --write` and a foreground read-only task with the prompt from the release run  complete (exit 0); the run's `--name` is the prefix and the start of the prompt with the quotes  gone (they become spaces, which `shorten` folds), and the prompt Copilot receives still holds the  quotes. These fail on the current code.- A background task with a `"` reaches job status `completed`, and its result holds no refusal  (fails on the current code).- `buildPersistentTaskThreadName` (exported) with U+0000, U+0001, U+0008, U+001F and U+007F (the  ends of the range and a control that is not white space) gives spaces in their place  (fails on the current code); with only `"` characters, an empty or white-space prompt, the bare  prefix `Copilot Companion Task` (the quote case fails on the current code); with 60 emoji, a name  of at most 100 UTF-16 units; with `'`, a backtick, `\` and non-ASCII letters, those characters  kept (these last two pass on the current code too; they guard the length rule and against a  filter that takes too much). **CHANGELOG**: a new `### 1.0.24` entry above `### 1.0.23`. It gives this fix and repeats the 1.0.23change, because 1.0.23 is not published and the release notes take only the 1.0.24 entry. The1.0.23 entry stays as it is. **Checks**: `npm ci --include=dev`, `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run check-version` and`claude plugin validate .`; CI on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows; after the merge, the release run, withstep 4's prompt holding double quotes again. ## Risks & Considerations - The probe ran on Windows only. The check is Copilot CLI's own, so macOS and Linux should give the  same answers, but CI uses the fake CLI and cannot show it.- A later Copilot CLI may refuse more characters. The fake CLI copies 1.0.95's rules, so a new rule  shows only in the release run or a user report.- Session names that users already have keep their quotes; only new tasks change.- Not an upstream defect: Codex's app server takes the name as is. ## Open Questions - None. ## Constitution Check - **I. Upstream parity**: met. `buildTaskThreadName` keeps upstream's name and shape; the filter is a  difference that Copilot CLI needs, recorded in the README section "Differences from the Codex  plugin" and the `copilot.mjs` header.- **II. Only reviewed code**: met. A regular expression; no new dependency.- **III. Copilot CLI through documented interfaces only**: met. `--name` stays; the plugin now passes  only values that Copilot CLI accepts.- **IV. Safe by default**: met. The prompt is unchanged; the name holds less.- **V. Cross-platform**: met. A string change; the tests run on all three systems in CI.- **VI. Tested, including failure paths**: met. The fake CLI refuses what the real one refuses, so  every task test checks the name; tests cover the quote, control characters, an empty excerpt, and  the characters that must stay. Patch release 1.0.24, whose `CHANGELOG.md` entry also gives the  unpublished 1.0.23 change, then the release run after the merge.

# Bug Fix: a task whose prompt holds a double quote fails before Copilot starts - **Slug**: 151-safe-session-name- **Fixed**: 2026-10-27- **Assessment**: ./assessment.md- **Status**: applied ## Summary `buildTaskThreadName` now puts a space in place of each `"` and each ASCII control character(U+0000 to U+001F, U+007F) before `shorten` folds and cuts the excerpt, so the session name holdsnothing that Copilot CLI 1.0.95 refuses. The prompt that Copilot receives is unchanged. ## Changes | File | Change | Notes ||------|--------|-------|| `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/copilot.mjs` | modified | The filter in `buildTaskThreadName`, with a comment; header comment || `tests/fake-copilot-fixture.mjs` | modified | The fake CLI refuses an empty `--name`, one over 100 characters, or one with `"` or an ASCII control character, after it writes its run record || `tests/copilot.test.mjs` | added tests | The name builder; the fake CLI's name rules || `tests/runtime-task.test.mjs` | added tests | Foreground (read-only and `--write`) and background tasks with a quoted prompt || `README.md` | modified | A "Differences from the Codex plugin" bullet || `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md` | modified | `### 1.0.24` entry, which also repeats the unpublished 1.0.23 change || `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `plugins/copilot/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | modified | `npm run bump-version -- 1.0.24` | ## Diff Highlights (optional) ```js// Copilot CLI refuses a --name that holds a double quote or an ASCII control character.function buildTaskThreadName(prompt) {  const excerpt = shorten(String(prompt ?? "").replace(/["\u0000-\u001f\u007f]/g, " "), 56);  return excerpt ? `${TASK_THREAD_PREFIX}: ${excerpt}` : TASK_THREAD_PREFIX;}``` ## Tests Added or Updated These fail on the old code: - `tests/runtime-task.test.mjs`, "a task whose prompt holds double quotes runs, and only its session  name loses them": the release run's prompt, read-only and `--write`, exit 0; the `--name` is  `Copilot Companion Task: Add the comment line // Checked by the release run. a...`; Copilot gets  the prompt with its quotes.- `tests/runtime-task.test.mjs`, "a background task whose prompt holds double quotes completes": job  status `completed`, the result is the answer with no refusal, and the prompt keeps its quotes.- `tests/copilot.test.mjs`, "a task's session name holds no character that Copilot CLI refuses, and  keeps the rest": U+0000, U+0001, U+0008, U+001F and U+007F become a space; `"` goes; a prompt of  only `""` gives the bare prefix. These pass on the old code too: - The same unit test: an empty or white-space prompt gives the bare prefix; 60 emoji give at most  100 UTF-16 units; `'`, a backtick, `\` and `café` stay.- `tests/copilot.test.mjs`, "the fake Copilot CLI refuses the session names that Copilot CLI 1.0.95  refuses": `a"b`, a tab, U+0001, U+007F, 101 characters, 60 emoji and an empty name give exit 1,  the real message and no output; `a'b`, `café` and 100 characters pass.- Every other task test now runs through the stricter fake CLI. ## Local Verification - Commands run: `npm run build` (pass), `npm test` (507 tests: 465 pass, 42 skipped, 0 fail),  `npm run check-version` (1.0.24), `claude plugin validate .` (pass).- Before the fix, the three tests listed as failing on the old code failed: the runtime ones with  the fake CLI's "Session name must not contain double quotes.", the unit one with the U+0000 kept. ## Deviations from Assessment - 2026-10-27: the foreground read-only test passes `--fresh` with the prompt. With one argument  after `task`, the companion splits it again like a shell line (`normalizeArgv`, open issue #111),  which drops every `"` before the prompt and the name are built. That is main's behaviour and #111's  scope. So a prompt given as one string never reached `--name` with its quotes; the failure hits a  prompt that comes with an option, as in the release run (`--background --write --json`), and  would hit every prompt once #111 is fixed. ## Follow-ups - #111 keeps the quotes of a one-string prompt; this fix keeps such a prompt's session name valid  then.
